title: GPU nodegroup Terraform module: unified ASG + Karpenter support for Private VPC
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: deliver a production-ready Terraform module that provisions GPU node groups inside a customer Private (VPC) Redwood Kubernetes deployment and supports both ASG-backed and Karpenter-backed autoscaling modes. The module must: 1) provide a clear, minimal API for customers to create GPU pools, 2) be idempotent and safe for in-place upgrades, 3) include automated health checks and remediation hooks, and 4) support a deterministic fallback path (ASG) when Karpenter is not available or for constrained environments.
acceptance_criteria:
- Terraform module variables and outputs are documented in module README and examples directory.
- Module can create either ASG-backed GPU nodegroup or configure labels/taints for Karpenter to claim GPU instances depending on `mode` variable.
- Upgrade test: rolling upgrade from ami v1 -> v2 with <5% pod disruption for real workload (integration test).
- Health checks: node-level and GPU driver checks exposed via Prometheus metrics and a remediation lambda/automation that cordons & replaces unhealthy nodes.
- CI: module runs `terraform validate`, `terraform plan` for examples, and a terratest e2e that provisions a tiny cluster using our private VPC sandbox.
- Documented rollback and drainage behavior in CONFLUENCE and linked runbook.
implementation_notes:
Design decisions: prefer a single module with `mode = "asg" | "karpenter"` to reduce duplication. For ASG mode we create Launch Template + ASG + Node IAM Role + NodeGroup autoscaling lifecycle hooks. For Karpenter mode module emits NodeClass / Provisioner manifest (templated) and IAM roles/instance profiles for allowed instance types. NodeImage and GPU driver bootstrapping use a user-data script stored in S3 or templated via cloud-init.
API surface (high level): variables: cluster_id, vpc_id, subnet_ids, mode, gpu_instance_types (list), gpu_min, gpu_max, desired_gpu, node_labels (map string->string), node_taints (list), node_ami, node_user_data_url, enable_gpu_driver (bool), upgrade_strategy (rolling|blue-green), max_unavailable (int), health_check_grace_period_seconds (int). outputs: nodegroup_ids, autoscaling_group_id, launch_template_id, provisioner_manifest_s3_url.
Upgrades: implement `upgrade_strategy=rolling` by creating a new launch template with new AMI and kicking instance refresh for ASG. For Karpenter use taint-based replacement: create new provisioner with label/taint and cordon old nodes; rely on pod disruption budgets and grace windows. Provide an explicit `drain_timeout` variable and integrate `kubectl drain` via automation job in CI/CD pipeline for controlled upgrades.
Fallback behaviour: when `mode=karpenter` but no capacity, we provide an example `asg_fallback` module invocation in examples that can be manually enabled by operators.
Security: node role limited via least-privilege policy (ECR pull, S3 get for userdata, CloudWatch/SSM if enabled). KMS keys for S3 userdata are supported.
testing_plan:
- Unit: terraform fmt + validate + static checks with tflint.
- Integration: terratest (Go) that provisions minimal GPU spot/ondemand instance type in sandbox VPC, runs a smoke job that loads TensorFlow and confirms GPU visibility (nvidia-smi), and tears down.
- E2E upgrade scenario test: provision nodegroup v1, schedule long-running docker job, perform module upgrade to v2 and assert zero data loss and <5% request errors.
- Health check test: simulate GPU driver crash (kill driver container) and assert automation cordons node and triggers replacement within grace_period.
- CI gating: PRs to /modules/gpu must pass terratest or be marked as non-blocking with explicit engineering approval for infra-only changes.
rollout_plan: Stage 1: land module and examples in `modules/gpu` with `mode=asg` default. Stage 2: enable `mode=karpenter` examples and add Provisioner templates. Stage 3: pilot with one customer Private deployment (non-critical tenant). Stage 4: opt-in rollout for new Private clusters. Each stage will be accompanied by a runbook describing manual steps, rollback instructions, and metrics to monitor (node replacement rate, GPU utilization, pod evictions).
observability: Expose node & GPU health metrics to Redwood Console via Prometheus exporter: node_gpu_driver_up (0/1), node_gpu_memory_total_bytes, node_gpu_memory_free_bytes, node_gpu_utilization_percent. Emit event on node cordon/drain with tags: module_key=ENG-10412, cluster, nodegroup. Integrate CloudWatch logs for ASG lifecycle hooks and Karpenter controller logs for provisioning failures. Create dashboard: Private -> Node Pools -> GPU Pool with graphs for node count, pending pods, average GPU utilization, replacement_rate, and last_health_check_status.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Karpenter provisioning times vary and can cause latency for bursty workloads. Mitigation: document burst capacity via pre-provisioned ASG fallback and recommend mixed instance types.
- Risk: improper upgrade may evict high-priority pods. Mitigation: require PDBs on critical workloads and `max_unavailable` defaults to 1 for GPU pools.
- Risk: GPU driver bootstrapping failures. Mitigation: bake GPU driver in AMI for production images and keep user-data fallback only for experimental AMIs; add smoke-check in cloud-init that fails instance launch if nvml not present.
- Risk: Terraform state drift for Karpenter provisioner manifests. Mitigation: store canonical manifest in S3 and manage via module outputs; provide `force_replace_provisioner` boolean when necessary.
